gen.title: How PCR copies DNA segments
gen.orderNote: Steps follow the order described in the how PCR works paragraph.

steps.label: Sample heated to denature DNA
steps.quote: To amplify a segment of DNA using PCR, the sample is first heated so the DNA denatures, or separates into two pieces of single-stranded DNA.

steps.label: Taq polymerase builds new strands
steps.quote: Next, an enzyme called "Taq polymerase" synthesizes - builds - two new strands of DNA, using the original strands as templates.

steps.label: Duplication creates molecules with old and new strands
steps.quote: This process results in the duplication of the original DNA, with each of the new molecules containing one old and one new strand of DNA.

steps.label: Strands create two new copies
steps.quote: Then each of these strands can be used to create two new copies, and so on, and so on.

steps.label: Cycle repeats to make many copies
steps.quote: The cycle of denaturing and synthesizing new DNA is repeated as many as 30 or 40 times, leading to more than one billion exact copies

steps.label: Thermocycler automates temperature changes
steps.quote: It is directed by a machine called a thermocycler, which is programmed to alter the temperature of the reaction every few minutes
